evals.prompt: We're adding a public API endpoint that lets a tenant admin invite new users by email. Threat-model this before we build it.
evals.expected_output: Should name concrete assets (tenant user list, invitation tokens, email addresses). Should identify the public API edge and the auth boundary (tenant-admin-only) as trust boundaries. Should walk STRIDE per boundary and produce at least 5 concrete threats with specific countermeasures (e.g. invitation token expiry/single-use, rate limiting invite sends, verifying the inviter is actually a tenant admin server-side not from a client claim). Should not produce vague 'validate input' style countermeasures.
assertions: Names concrete assets, not vague ones
Produces at least 5 threats across STRIDE categories
Each threat has a specific, mechanism-level countermeasure
Does not invent unrelated threats with no connection to the feature

evals.prompt: Fill in the Threat Model section for a feature that only touches internal batch-processing code with no external API and no user-facing surface.
evals.expected_output: Should still produce a threat model but scope it honestly to what's real: internal actors, queue/job boundaries, data-at-rest tampering by another internal service. Should not force public-API-style threats (spoofing external users) that don't apply, and should say so explicitly rather than padding the count.
assertions: Does not invent external-user threats for an internal-only system
Explicitly states which STRIDE categories don't apply and why
Still finds real internal trust boundaries (e.g. queue consumer, other internal services)
Doesn't pad the threat count with weak/generic entries just to hit 5
